newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan bourse ends session a shade higher.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan bourse ends session a shade higher.

text.p: The Casablanca stock exchange closed on Wednesday 0.64 percent higher on increasing demands for blue-chip stocks, a market analyst said.
The all-share index closed at 474.25 points from 471.18 points on the previous session.
"The market pursues its upward trend because there is an increasing demand for the market blue chips such as ONA Group and Wafabank," a broker at Upline Securities said.
He said an estimated 6,500 shares were exchanged on the official market during the bourse two-hour session on Wednesday.
ONA group, the country's largest conglomerate, rose for the third consecutive day to close at 593 dirhams, up 11 dirhams over the previous trading.
The conglomerate expects more than 720 million dirhams net profits in 1996.
Its subsidiary Centrale Laitiere, jumped 56 dirhams to close at 1,916 dirhams compared with the previous session.
Wafabank, one of the market blue chips, gained nine dirhams to close at 580 dirhams.
Wafabank decided to buy 100 percent of Spanish Uniban bank or more than 2.46 million shares priced at around $28 million, a bourse official said.
Uniban is expected to hold its general assembly on Thursday to confirm the merger with Wafabank, a Uniban spokesman said.
Wafabank is offering one share in exchange for five shares of Uniban while shareholders wanted one share against four, the broker added.
The effective absorption of Uniban by Wafabank will take place by end March 1997, a Wafabank official said.
Eqdom, a leading credit firm which was recently privatised, rose 28 dirhams to close at 964 dirhams.
Traded volume on the official market was 36.7 million dirhams compared with 37.6 million dirhams on Tuesday.
